attributes.body:
Arize and Dynatrace: making the World's AI Work.

Published august 13, 2026.

Aparna and I started Arize 6+ years ago with a simple proposition that headlined its seed deck:

"We Make the World's AI Work"

Today Arize is announcing the signing of a definitive agreement for the acquisition of Arize by Dynatrace to accelerate that proposition.

Arize made a bet years ago that the explosion of AI would require bespoke infra tools. Arize knew AI systems weren't going to behave like traditional software because Arize were building systems approaching human-level reasoning, the next generation of intelligence. The visibility into why something failed simply wasn't going to be as straightforward or as consistent.

That bet became the market's first AI Observability platform, and with it, AI evaluations were born. Arize also bet that orders of magnitude more AI products would ship and that thousands of them would see the light of production. Arize believed so deeply in the importance of this problem Arize named the company Arize, symbolizing its mission to stand up AI and bring it to life in the real world.

Fast forward to 2026. The world has changed dramatically. Every company in the world is scaling up its use of agents, AI is everywhere and agents are reshaping business after business.

What wasn't clear years ago and is crystal clear today is that agent systems and software are joined at the hip.

* The best general agents are coding agents.
* Skills and tools for agents are mixtures of prompts and code.
* Prompts that control agents live in the code repo.
* The logs and traces used to debug your software also help you debug your AI systems.
* The path to AGI is likely through coding agents.

AI and software systems are deeply connected together in ways that none of Arize fathomed.

Where is AI going?

Agents are transforming the Observability market from measurement to action.

Arize is moving to a world where AI and software systems will continually improve autonomously. The foundation for continuous improvement is the data that describes what your system did - logs and traces - which will guide agents as they take action to fix systems.

The markets for Observability and AI Observability are converging.

* For agents to continuously improve systems, software will need to trace 100x more data than today. For this to work, every inch of software needs to be logged for agents to truly make continuous fixes.
* AI Observability is transforming measurement into action by adding long running agents to fix your systems (Arize Signal and Arize Managed Agents). All of these agents are driven by data from Observability infrastructure.

Arize was built as an agent-first platform, with one of the largest collections of agent trace data in the industry. Dynatrace brings depth in tracing and logging software systems that provide the data to drive these agents. These two areas just belong together if Arize is going to build the future systems that continuously improve.

Some thank you's.

Before I talk about what's next, some thank you's.

To the Arize team. Startups are hard in normal markets. Arize built infrastructure for a market that kept changing under its feet, and this team kept listening to customers, kept shipping, and kept believing. You turned an idea into the category leader. I could not be prouder of you.

To Aparna. For six years Arize has worked on this product nonstop, through every stage of company-building and life. You never slowed down and never stopped raising the bar. There is no Arize without Aparna. I couldn't have built this with anyone else.

To its customers, who have trusted Arize with their most important AI systems before this category existed. You have made the product better every single day.

To its investors, advisors, and early believers who backed Arize when AI observability was not a budget line or even a real category yet. Thank you investors and board - Brett Wilson (Swift Ventures), Ashu Garg (Foundation Capital), Dharmesh Thakker (Battery), Morgan Gerlak (TCV), and John Cordo (Evolution).

Jason Mendel and Jaya Gupta have been instrumental in its journey in so many ways. These folks behind the scenes help so many companies in so many ways.

And to the open source community around Phoenix and OpenInference. Developer trust and open standards are the foundation this category gets built on.

I keep thinking back to the beginning. Arize started as an InVision prototype and a small group of people who believed AI was going to need this before the market did. No category, no budget lines, no playbook. Just a demo and a conviction that production AI was coming and somebody had to make it work. Most of those people are still here. That's the part I'm proudest of.

Where does the industry go.

There will be a time very soon where a single business will run more than a million agents. The challenge for that business will be making sure those agents are making the correct decisions, operating securely and not doing anything you don't want them to do.

That is why Arize exist.

Its internal "full" mission statement since the founding has been:

"We Make the World's AI Work and Work for The 'People"

The "Work for the People" has meant a number of things over the years. But today, as we look at this industry on the edge of a new era, "for the people" clearly means the safety and security of agents.

Arize collects billions of agent trajectory events and Arize has a unique view into agents' actions. Dynatrace tracks everything your software does. Making AI work and making it work securely requires many things each company uniquely does today.

The power of connecting Arize and Dynatrace is the potential to truly deliver on the vision Arize started the company with years ago. Excited for the next chapter!

attributes.body:
Arize AI acquires Velvet.

Media contacts.

Addition to accelerate developer-first AI infrastructure.

Berkeley, CA - March 13, 2025 - Arize, a leader in AI observability and LLM evaluation, today announced the acquisition of Velvet, a developer-first AI gateway startup.

Arize helps organizations ensure AI systems work reliably in production through advanced testing, model monitoring, evaluation frameworks, and debugging tools. The platform supports AI agents, voice assistants, and other sophisticated gen-AI applications as well as traditional ML. Velvet provides developers with lightweight tooling to analyze, evaluate, and monitor AI features.

"We're thrilled to welcome the Velvet team and work toward a shared vision around AI observability," said Jason Lopatecki, CEO and Co-Founder of Arize AI.

The Velvet team will focus on developer experience initiatives, helping to accelerate adoption of Arize's unified AI platform, spanning:

Arize AX for Enterprise - AI evaluation and observability platform

Arize Phoenix OSS - Open-source AI observability with 2M+ monthly downloads

Arize AI Copilot - An AI-powered agent that helps engineers debug, optimize, and analyze models faster with 30+ skills.

"Joining Arize lets us bring sophisticated AI infrastructure to more full-stack product developers," said Emma Lawler, former CEO of Velvet. "Our shared vision is to make AI observability accessible while maintaining the enterprise-grade capabilities teams need as they scale."

Chris Hendel, Velvet's co-founder and CTO, will lead platform engineering initiatives at Arize. Velvet's existing customers will have the option to transition to Arize's platform.

About Arize
Arize AI is a unified AI observability and LLM evaluation platform that helps teams develop and maintain more successful AI. Arize's automated monitoring and observability platform allows teams to quickly detect issues when they emerge, troubleshoot why they happened, and improve overall performance across both traditional ML and generative use cases. Arize is headquartered in Berkeley, CA.

About Velvet
Velvet provides an AI gateway to help developers analyze, evaluate, and monitor AI features in production. The product enables teams to seamlessly observe LLM requests, analyze performance, and continuously test AI features with minimal setup overhead.

attributes.body:
Acuity Brands to acquire horticultural brand from Current.

Deal between rivals enhances Acuity's portfolio. Current exits horticultural lighting sector.

Acuity Brands, North America's largest lighting company, has agreed to acquire the Arize(R) family of horticulture lighting products from rival Current Lighting Solutions, a $1 billion competitor in commercial lighting. This acquisition, coupled with a distribution agreement with Hort Americas, LLC, marks a substantial expansion in Acuity Brands' product offerings in the controlled environment agriculture market. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

In 2022, Acuity Brands introduced the Verjure(TM) brand, a professional-grade horticulture LED lighting solution. This series, developed through extensive plant-based academic research, supports all stages of plant growth in various indoor settings such as warehouses, greenhouses, and vertical racks. The acquisition of the Arize(R) product line from Current Lighting Solutions adds depth to Acuity's offering, enhancing the company's position in the horticulture lighting market.

Acuity Brands and Hort Americas partnership.

In addition to the Arize product line acquisition, Acuity Brands reached an agreement with Hort Americas for it to remain as the exclusive distributor of these horticulture lighting products throughout the U.S., Canada, and Mexico.

Tony Gineris, VP & General Manager of Industrial and Outdoor at Acuity Brands Lighting and Lighting Controls, emphasized the strategic nature of these agreements. He stated that incorporating high-powered, greenhouse-focused luminaires into Acuity Brands' portfolio will allow the company to expand its offerings in the fast-growing controlled environment agriculture market. Gineris also highlighted the synergy between Acuity Brands' lighting and controls expertise and Hort Americas' established presence in the commercial greenhouse space.

Competitive dynamics:

This development enhances competition in the horticulture lighting sector. Acuity Brands' rival, Signify, acquired Austin, Texas-based Fluence in 2022 for $272 million. The acquisition aimed to strengthen Signify's horticultural lighting business, especially in North America. Before the acquisition, Fluence reported revenues of $141 million. The global horticultural lighting market was projected to reach $1.8 billion by 2024, but recent quarterly earnings reports from the company have indicated a slowdown in the sector.

Category Exit for Current: The decision to spin off Arize marks Current's exit from the horticultural lighting category. A company spokesperson shared, "Horticulture will not be a strategic focus for us moving forward as we have reached an agreement to transfer the technology to Acuity. Our focus will be on continued efforts to merge the GE Current, a Daintree Company and Hubbell Lighting businesses, systems and portfolios, offering first in class service to our customers with a laser focus in the C&I, Roadway, Distribution and Specialty channels across luminaires and controls."

Acuity Brands' transaction with Current is expected to be finalized by the end of January 2024. Post-acquisition, the Arize products will join Acuity Brands' Verjure(TM) series of horticulture lighting products. The agreement with Hort Americas will be activated upon the closure of the transaction with Current.

This acquisition positions Acuity Brands as a stronger player in the North American horticulture lighting market.
